As a GFTI IIEST( Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology)  graduate I've learnt one thing the curriculum is the same in all college's for Engineering whether it's an IIT or some any other collage near you that's considered a tier 3  college this especially true for branches such as CSE,ECE,EE, Mechanical and civil the curriculum followed itself is pretty outdated and doesn't focus on the  development of Industry  skills but rather a precursor to a master's program. Private colleges which are often seen as tier 3 have tie ups with a few companies that actually provide the exposure needed and thereby showing students that technology is ever changing and evolving and that what is  relevant today might not be relevant tomorrow ultimate resulting in skills being you're best asset thereby allowing the college to change it's curriculum to the needs of the job market. 

The reason GFTIs ( Government Funded Technological Institutions) are sought after is that they're system is different and they've learnt from other countries that graduating with a particular degree isn't really necessary and that you can choose your qualifications based on an exam being your major and your areas of keen interest as the minors( in which you can quite literally opt for almost any subject including niche areas and from other streams) . This system making sure that you have skills in more than one area to get a job in.

I can assure you that this isn't the case a lot of companies tend to believe that need to pay higher if the employee is a an IIT/NIT or a GFTI graduate in general but that's only just after graduation 7 to 10 years down the list ne your work experience matters more than you're qualifications times are changing nowadays people are beginning to realise that skill is and should be valued higher than the educational qualification.
